summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and esophageal varices, was admitted for evaluation of hematemesis and melena. Initial workup revealed a drop in hemoglobin from baseline, leading to concern for upper gastrointestinal bleeding. He was started on octreotide, pantoprazole, and ceftriaxone, and underwent an endoscopy which showed no active bleeding but confirmed grade one esophageal varices. A urinary tract infection due to Enterococcus was identified and treated with a seven-day course of amoxicillin. Due to a history of positive syphilis serology and behavioral concerns, a lumbar puncture was performed; cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed no signs of neurosyphilis, though confirmatory results remained pending at discharge. The patient was monitored for alcohol withdrawal using the CIWA scale but did not require treatment. He was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, undergo a repeat endoscopy in eight weeks, and follow up with his primary care and liver specialists. Medication adjustments included holding lisinopril and furosemide, switching nadolol to bedtime dosing, and adding folic acid.
